items.title: Rename the usage log and its schema to agent_usage (issue #192)
items.action:
1. `git mv docs/_harness/pr_review_agent_usage.jsonl docs/_harness/agent_usage.jsonl` (rows unchanged: history).
2. `git mv plugins/harness/schemas/pr_review_agent_usage.schema.json plugins/harness/schemas/agent_usage.schema.json`; set `$id` to the new file name and `title` to `Agent Usage`. Keep every rule; the description keeps its meaning (TASK-4 widens the rules).

3b. `.claude/harness.json`: add `"agent_usage_path": "docs/_harness/agent_usage.jsonl"` in the same commit as the `git mv`. This repo's sessions run the published (main) pr-review-watch 0.5.1, which reads that key, so its next row lands in the new log instead of recreating the old one. items.title: Split agent-watcher into a generic core and a pr-review layer, behavior unchanged
items.action:
Layout (D1 io-closures, D7 direct-register):
- `hooks/register.ts`: the composition root, the only file importing both sides: `registerCore(on, LAYERS)` then `registerPrReviewLayer(on)`; `LAYERS` from `hooks/layers/index.ts`.
- `hooks/core/`: `layer.ts` (the `Layer` and `Io` types), `watch.ts`, `root.ts`, `config.ts` (state_dir, agent_usage_path; exports the parsed harness.json object for layers), `contract.ts` (header parse, return block, DEFINED_AGENTS, standalone ids, model family), `usageRow.ts`, `jsonl.ts` (appendValid, readJsonl, recordFailures), `tracker.ts` (Agent dispatch, loop ids, usage folding, usage append, the Stop/refresh fan-out to layers).
- `hooks/layers/pr-review/`: `identify.ts` (RUN_ID/MODE/AGENT_ROLE header, MODES), `runKey.ts`, `sentinels.ts`, `phase5Scan.ts`, `bubbles.ts`, `matrixRow.ts`, `runs.ts` (phase, bubbled, settle, band text), `band.tsx`, `config.ts` (matrix_path, artifacts.reviews, artifacts.scratch, base_branch), `layer.ts` (`prReviewLayer` and `registerPrReviewLayer(on)`).
Interface: `Layer = { name; identify(subagentType, header) => Claim | undefined; rowFields?(io, run, agent, completion) => Promise<FixerCounts-like extras>; onSettle?(io, run) => Promise<void>; stopReason?(io, stop) => Promise<string | undefined>; resultContext?(io, run, agent, result) => Promise<string[]> }`. Core appends what `resultContext` returns to the Agent tool result's `context`, in the same hook and order as `tracker.ts:571-573` today; `OWNER_NOTE` and `ownsRows` move to `hooks/layers/pr-review/layer.ts`, whose `resultContext` returns the note for a pr-review reviewer of a run recorded with a PR number. Pure functions take no `$`; anything needing the host takes `io`, built by a core function declaration `ioOf($)` (readText, listDir, exists, write, gitLine, toast, now, and the state reads and updates the layer needs). Layer hooks that the engine raises on their own (ui.render AbovePrompt, prompt.submit PHASE5_PENDING, session.end, session.compact, Bash/PowerShell refresh after `pr_review.py`, session.start pr-team recovery) are registered inside `registerPrReviewLayer(on)`.
Rules: no file under `hooks/core/` imports from `hooks/layers/`. Keep today's order inside one hook: record the dispatch or completion, then the layer settles (refresh, matrix flush), as `tracker.ts:566-573` and `:596-601` do now. Run-level pr-review data (pr, phase, runtimeDir, bubbled, bubbledFrom, verdict) may stay on `Run` as optional layer-owned fields, or move to a layer atom declared in `types/index.d.ts`; either way the state contract keeps every value it holds today. Functions taking `$` stay function declarations (`phase5Scan.ts:11`).
Tests: each `*.test.ts` moves beside its file; the end-to-end `tracker.test.ts` and `band.test.tsx` stay at `hooks/`. No test is dropped or weakened: the total stays at least 164. `config.test.ts` splits with `config.ts`: each case goes with the key it covers (`core/config.test.ts`, `layers/pr-review/config.test.ts`); the mirror test reads both config files. Update the path constants in `tests/mods/test_agent_watcher_*.py`, `test_local_run_key_mirror.py` and `tests/skills/test_bubble_memo_agents_contract.py`. Outside references to moved files: `plugins/bubble-stamp/hooks/review.ts:3` (bubbles.ts), `.claude/skills/porting-into-straps/SKILL.md` (the mod's config.ts / root.ts patterns) and `CLAUDE.md` (the mirror rule names agent-watcher's `hooks/core/config.ts` and `hooks/layers/pr-review/config.ts`). README: a Layout section (core, the Layer and Io contract, adding a layer). Copy the planned `tests/mods/test_agent_watcher_layers.py`.

items.title: Generic tracking: every dispatch, the header convention and open row fields (issue #193)
items.action:
1. Core tracks every Agent call (D5): drop the `isDefinedAgent` gate in `trackedDispatch`; a call no layer claims is a generic run of one. `DEFINED_AGENTS` stays as data (its contract test stays); built-ins and other plugins' agents log with `subagent_type` as given and `agent_id` the type's name after any plugin prefix (`general-purpose` when the call names none).
2. Header convention: parse the leading block (D3) of uppercase `KEY: value` / `KEY=value` lines. Core reads the D2 skill key, `RUN_ID`, `AGENT_ROLE`, `AGENT_ID` and `PR` (`AGENT_ROLE` is the key the pr-review and pr-team headers and return blocks already use). Layers still claim first (pr-review and pr-team headers unchanged), with one change (D9): the pr-review layer's `identify` refuses a header whose skill key is present and is neither `pr-review` nor `pr-team`, so a skill that prints `RUN_ID`, `AGENT_ID` and `AGENT_ROLE: reviewer` under its own `SKILL:` line is a generic row, never a pr-team run. For an unclaimed dispatch every consumed value falls back instead of failing the row (D11), so D5's "every dispatch is logged" holds: skill from the key with a leading `<plugin>:` stripped, kept only when it matches SKILL_PATTERN (else `standalone`); role from AGENT_ROLE when it matches ROLE_PATTERN and is not `fixer` or `closer` (else `other`; those two need the counts only a layer computes); run_id from RUN_ID and agent_id from AGENT_ID unless the value holds `/` or `\` (D8 applied to the columns), else the generated `standalone_<UTC>_<seq>` and the type name; pr from PR when it is a positive integer (else null). A raw value that fell back stays in `fields` under its key, subject to D8. 2b. Claim marker (D10): `Run` records the layer that claimed it (`claimedBy?: string`, unset for a generic run). The band's `activeAtom` write, the post-dispatch layer refresh and the after-row drop test that flag instead of `skill === 'standalone'` (today `tracker.ts:184`, `:190`, `:569`, now in `core/tracker.ts`). An unclaimed dispatch's state entry is keyed by its generated `standalone_<UTC>_<seq>` id whatever its header RUN_ID, so parallel dispatches that share a RUN_ID keep separate entries and each logs its own row.
3. Rows of an unclaimed dispatch gain an optional `fields` object: every leading-block key core did not consume, value as written (trimmed). D8: a value holding a path separator (`/` or `\`) is dropped with its key, so no local or absolute path reaches the log; any other value is cut to 200 characters (197 and `...`). Absent when empty. A layer-claimed row carries no `fields`, so pr-review and pr-team rows stay exactly as they are. pr and the fixer counts stay top-level.
4. Schema `agent_usage.schema.json`: `skill` becomes a string with pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` (pr-review, pr-team, standalone still valid); `role` a string with pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$` (the six current roles still valid); add `fields` (object, propertyNames `^[A-Z][A-Z_]*$`, string values with maxLength 200 and pattern `^[^/\\]*$`, no path separator); `signal` description: `NO_BLOCK` when the agent returned without a return block, no standalone framing; title and description name every Agent dispatch. Old rows still validate.
5. TS validator `core/usageRow.ts` follows the schema: drop the USAGE_SKILLS and USAGE_ROLES enums for the two patterns (export them as SKILL_PATTERN and ROLE_PATTERN), allow and check `fields`. Update `tests/mods/test_agent_watcher_usage_contract.py` to pin the patterns and the `fields` rule instead of the enums.
6. TS tests: a built-in dispatch logs a row; a header with the skill key, RUN_ID and extra keys logs skill, run_id and fields; a prompt whose header block ends before a body `SIGNAL:` line keeps that line out of fields; a pr-review slot dispatch logs exactly as before, with no `fields` key; a value over 200 characters is cut; a strap runner header (TREE, INIT) and a bubble-memo FILES line log no `/` or `\` anywhere in the row's `fields`. Review 0208 cases: a header with `SKILL: bubble-memo`, RUN_ID, AGENT_ID and `AGENT_ROLE: reviewer` logs skill `bubble-memo` as a generic row with no matrix row, no band change and no pr-team run; `SKILL: harness:strap-skills` logs skill `strap-skills`; `SKILL: Strap Skills` logs `standalone` with `fields.SKILL`; an unclaimed `AGENT_ROLE: fixer` logs role `other`; `AGENT_ID: docs/x` and `RUN_ID: a/b` fall back to the type name and the generated id; `PR: 208` fills `pr`; a `SKILL: strap-skills` dispatch leaves the band's active run unchanged and its run is gone from state after its usage row; two concurrent dispatches under one RUN_ID log two rows.
7. Root `README.md` (lines 40 and 429 describe the defined-agent gate): every Agent dispatch is logged. Mod README: the header convention, `fields`, and that every dispatch is logged. `tests/schemas/test_agent_usage_schema.py`: drop the `unknown-skill` and `unknown-role` rejection cases (now valid). Copy the planned `tests/schemas/test_agent_usage_open_rows.py`.

decisions.question: How does a layer reach the engine (`$`) when the core calls it?

options.summary: Layer methods take `$` and core passes it: `layer.onSettle($, run)`
Core builds an `Io` object of closures over `$` (read, list, write, toast, state update) and passes that; layers never see `$`

decisions.rationale: Spike on 2026-11-04 (`claude plugin validate` on a two-file probe mod): `layer.viaDecl?.($)` is refused with "$ itself is passed as an argument"; an `Io` built by a core function declaration and passed to `layer.rowFields(io, ...)` validates, reported as `$.fs.read (via ioOf)`.

decisions.question: Which header key names the dispatching skill, given that strap rows already print `SKILL: <skill under test>` and the strap agents read that line?

options.summary: `SKILL:` names the dispatching skill; strap's current `SKILL:` line is renamed `TARGET:` in strap.py, both strap agents and their init commands
A new key (for example `HARNESS_SKILL:`) names the dispatching skill; strap's `SKILL:` line stays and lands in `fields`
`SKILL:` is read as written; strap rows log the skill under test as `skill`

decisions.rationale: Developer, 2026-11-04: `SKILL:` names the dispatching skill, as #193's example reads; strap's skill-under-test line becomes `TARGET:`.

decisions.question: Which prompt lines become a usage row's `fields`?

options.summary: The run of uppercase `KEY: value` (or `KEY=value`) lines at the top of the prompt, ending at the first line that is not one
Every column-1 uppercase key line anywhere in the prompt

decisions.rationale: Long prompts and briefs carry `SIGNAL:`-style lines in their body; only the leading block is the dispatch header.

decisions.question: Mixed-case prompt keys (todo-edit and sync-gh-todo `Operation:`/`Project root:`, docstring rows `Project root:`/`Scope:`, bubble-memo `Memo:`): rename to uppercase or leave?

options.summary: Leave them; drivers and skill prose only add the D2 skill line; mixed-case lines are not captured in `fields`
Rename every key to uppercase in drivers, skill prose and the agent files that read them, so they are captured

decisions.rationale: Developer, 2026-11-04: agent prompt contracts stay unchanged; only the skill line is added.

decisions.question: Which `Agent` dispatches does agent-watcher log?

options.summary: Every Agent call: defined agents, built-ins (Explore, general-purpose, Plan) and other plugins' agents
Only agents the marketplace defines (today's DEFINED_AGENTS rule)

decisions.rationale: Developer, 2026-11-03: agent-watcher "monitors and logs ALL agent dispatches".

decisions.question: Which return-block form does the watcher read?

options.summary: One form: the column-1 `---` fenced block with a SIGNAL line; strap runner and judge adopt it
Also accept a ```text fence
Leave strap rows at NO_BLOCK

decisions.rationale: Developer, 2026-11-03: "using the same form makes sense".

decisions.question: How do layer hooks (band, Stop, prompt line, shell refresh, session-start recovery) register?

options.summary: register.ts calls each layer's `registerXLayer(on)` function directly
register.ts loops over LAYERS and calls `layer.register(on)`

decisions.rationale: Spike on 2026-11-04: `layer.register?.(on)` is refused with "on is used other than as a call or an argument to a function of the module's own"; a direct `registerProbeHooks(on)` validates.

decisions.question: How are `fields` values stored in the tracked usage log, given that headers carry paths (strap TREE, INIT, SPEC; bubble-memo FILES)?

options.summary: As written, cut to 200 characters; paths enter the log
Core drops keys known to hold paths (TREE, INIT)
Core drops any value holding a path separator (`/` or `\`), key included; other values cut to 200 characters

decisions.rationale: Developer, 2026-11-04: "We do not want any local OR absolute paths" in the log. A generic rule on the value catches every key, known or not; the schema rejects a separator so a row that slips one through fails validation. The cap bounds row size (local review 1123, I4).

decisions.question: Which dispatches may the pr-review layer claim once any skill may print RUN_ID, AGENT_ID and AGENT_ROLE?

options.summary: identify refuses a header whose SKILL is present and not pr-review or pr-team
Reserve reviewer and fixer for the layer in the header convention; core logs a SKILL header before the layer claim

decisions.rationale: Review 0208 I2: today a RUN_ID + AGENT_ID + reviewer header with no PR line is claimed as pr-team. pr-review and pr-team headers carry no SKILL line, so refusing a foreign one changes nothing for them. Developer, 2026-11-04: amend and refreeze.

decisions.question: How does core tell a layer-claimed run from a generic one, and how are generic runs keyed?

options.summary: Run.claimedBy names the claiming layer; generic runs keyed by their generated id
Keep skill === 'standalone' as the marker

decisions.rationale: Review 0208 I2: once the skill comes from the SKILL header, the 'standalone' sentinel no longer marks unclaimed runs (band takeover, leaked runs, shared RUN_ID entries dropped early). Developer, 2026-11-04: amend and refreeze.

decisions.question: What does core do with a header value that fails its pattern or rule?

options.summary: Fall back (standalone, other, generated id, type name, null pr); a `<plugin>:` skill prefix is stripped; the raw value stays in fields under D8
Widen the schema patterns to the values real headers carry
Reject the row (as first planned)

decisions.rationale: Review 0208 I2: a rejected row breaks D5. Developer, 2026-11-04: strip the plugin prefix (`harness:strap-skills` logs `strap-skills`), schema skill pattern unchanged; PR fills the top-level pr; RUN_ID and AGENT_ID fall under the no-paths rule.
